newsitem.title: USA: Port of Charleston, S.C., sets cargo record.
newsitem.headline: Port of Charleston, S.C., sets cargo record.

text.p: Port of Charleston, S.C., handled a record 10.4 million tons of cargo in the year ended June 30, surpassing Oakland, Calif., as the nation's fifth busiest container port, the Post and Courier reported Friday.
The total for fiscal 1997 represents a 15 percent gain over last year.

The number of vessels arriving at Charleston's port increased by four percent to 1,740 for the year. The port handles an average of $65 million worth of cargo and five ships daily, according to the South Carolina Ports Authority.
The authority's three terminals in Charleston, Georgetown and Port Royal handled a combined total of 24 billion pounds of cargo in fiscal 1997, also a record, according to the Post and Courier.
